messages:
Alice: heads-up — after yesterday's continuous-batcher tweak (max_wait -> 10ms, stronger seq_len bucketing) Canary showed p99 up ~12% for short prompts and prefix cache hit-rate fell ~18%. sample flame & counts below, tilted toward more cache misses. anyone else seeing this?

Ben: hm. that sounds like batch composition changed in a way that mixes prefixes more. did we change cache key derivation too or just scheduler? :thinking:

Dmitri: only the scheduler. key derivation stayed as `sha256(prefix_bytes) + model+quant` AFAIK. the new max_wait reduces time to assemble a batch which increases the chance of combining different prefixes that previously waited for similar session traffic. result: fewer repeated prefixes per batch, so less KV reuse across microbatches.

Carol: quick numbers from the Canary window (last 6h):
- overall reqs: 1.2M
- prefix_cache_hit_rate: 82% -> 67% (pre->post)
- avg tokens served from cache per hit: 18 -> 12
- batch size mean: 4.8 -> 5.6 (weirder mix: stdev up)

Eve: interesting that batch size went up but hit-rate went down — implies batch composition diversity increased. maybe long prefixes are now polling less and getting mixed with many short cached prefixes so the cache warmups are ineffective.

Ben: would love to see per-batch prefix-id cardinality histogram (how many distinct prefix hashes per batch). if that spikes, it's our culprit. Also check queueing time distribution: lower max_wait can increase cold-starts if the cache isn't warmed.

perf-bot: Canary alert: prefix_cache_hit_rate dropped from 0.82 to 0.67 (delta -0.15) between 1767920000 and 1768004320. p99_latency_short_prompts increased by 12%.

Dmitri: propose two quick experiments:
1) revert max_wait to 30ms on Canary to confirm correlation.
2) add a small heuristic to the scheduler to prefer grouping by `prefix_hash` when possible (i.e., soft affinity) — cheaply computed and shouldn't blow up latency.

Carol: alternative: change cache keying to be less strict — e.g., strip session-scoped salts or trailing tokens that differ across requests. but that risks incorrect reuse if prefixes aren't actually equivalent. need careful eval.

Eve: another idea: implement a separate "cached-pref" fast-path queue. when a request matches a known-hot prefix (top N by freq in last window) route it to a short-latency cohort where we wait a bit longer to accumulate same-prefix requests. non-hot prefixes keep the aggressive max_wait. cheap to experiment with: maintain a small LRU of hot prefix hashes updated from metrics.

Ben: +1 for cheap fast-path. I'll also add instrumentation: per-batch {distinct_prefix_count, top_prefix_fraction, batch_age_ms} and a histogram of per-request wait-to-dispatch. that should show whether affinity grouping would help.

Alice: sounds good. timeline? can we get experiment 1 (revert max_wait) within today and boot instrumentation for 2 within 24h?

Dmitri: I can revert on Canary now. will post results in an hour.

Ben: I'll push metrics PR with new batch labels (batch.affinity_count, batch.top_prefix_pct) — ETA 4h. also adding a Grafana panel.

Eve: I'll prototype the hot-prefix queue as a flag in the scheduler (`hot_prefix_fastpath: true`) w/ config snippet:
```yaml
batcher:
  max_wait_ms: 10
  hot_prefix_fastpath: true
  hot_prefix_threshold: 1000  # requests in last hour
  hot_queue_wait_ms: 30
```
This keeps aggressive batching for cold traffic and waits slightly longer when we know the prefix is hot to raise hit rate.

Carol: please also capture kernel-selection traces in the batch profiler; if the batch composition change causes different kernel choices we could be doing more expensive kernels for small microbatches. put a tag per-batch: `kernel_variant`.

perf-bot: note added to Canary runbook: capture `batch.distinct_prefix_count`, `batch.top_prefix_pct`, `kernel_variant`, `prefix_cache_hit_rate` for every deploy.

Alice: great. once we have data from revert + metrics we'll pick between scheduler affinity vs hot-queue vs loosening cache keys. thanks all. :thumbsup:

Ben: on it. will post early numbers when available.

Dmitri: revert applied, traffic switching now. will report at +1h.

Carol: thanks — I'll pause the rollout to prod until we have confirmation.

Eve: if we need a quick mitigation in prod, hot-prefix fastpath is low-risk toggle.

Alice: ack.
